# `bin/claims-extract`

A tool: run it from the root of an instance (or of the kit, for the kit's own tools).
Source: [`bin/claims-extract`](../../../bin/claims-extract)

## What it says about itself

```text
bin/claims-extract [--through C-NNN] [--ids C-NNN ...] [--library PREFIX ...] [--supplied PREFIX=PATH ...] [--date YYYY-MM-DD]
                   [--out FILE]

The worker's view of the ledger (LESSONS.md "A worker's extract of the ledger is made by a tool"). A worker never receives
CLAIMS.md (bin/new-run refuses it); it receives this extract, made by fixed rules so that it is reproducible:
  kept      every entry no later entry supersedes, less the instance's excluded entries; for each, its header line verbatim,
            its statement verbatim, "Lean declarations: …" (a lean artifact) or "Artifact type: …", and its Claimed,
            Premises and Supersedes lines where it has them (bin/ledger-claims writes these lines)
  notes     the notes on kept entries, verbatim, in ledger order, less the instance's excluded notes, after the entries
  left out  superseded entries; every other line of an entry (artifact paths and hashes, deps, range, coverage,
            evidence, counter pressure, nonrigorous step, must show, silent links, check, prose, referee)
  header    the date, the entry range and counts, what is left out, and where the declarations are: PREFIX.* in the
            linked library for each --library; PREFIX.* at PATH for each --supplied; every other prefix "not supplied"
The exclusions are the user's, in data/packet-rules.json under "extract" (bin/packet-block --extract C-NNN,
--extract-note C-NNN DATE; the hook keeps the orchestrator out of both): for instance the entries of a heuristic model
whose probabilities no worker should receive. The extract names what it leaves out by id and date, never the why. --through C-NNN reads the ledger as it stood
when C-NNN was its last entry. --ids C-NNN ... extracts exactly those entries, superseded or not (a claim's `ledger`
premises name what it rests on; a superseded one is marked "Superseded by: …"), by the same rules and exclusions: what
bin/new-run gives a referee of such a claim as input/ledger-premises.md (LESSONS.md "A referee is given the ledger entries a
claim rests on"). Prints to stdout, or writes FILE (then one CLAIMS-EXTRACT ledger line with its sha256).
Read-only otherwise. The extract is a packet file: bin/lint-brief scans it with the rest. KIT_ROOT points it at a fixture tree.
```

## Lessons it cites

- → **A worker's extract of the ledger is made by a tool**
- → **A referee is given the ledger entries a claim rests on**

## Ledger events it writes

- `CLAIMS-EXTRACT`
